Sometimes this meant the system clock effectively skipped past the alarm during this period of being out of sync. Alarmy devs: to avoid this, sync once to ntp per boot, then use monotonic clock from that baseline.

text: I'm the heaviest sleeper I know. I was late to work 5 days a week. I've lost early morning flights. I'd rather not sleep and go live on early flights or meetings. I can sleep through the loudest stock alarms, beeps, vibrations, hard rock songs. I even bought an expensive wristband that literally gives you electrical shocks, and it worked for 1 week, then my wrist got used to those shocks! It is fun for the anecdotes, but really frustrating and unacceptable for a grown man to go through this. Alarmy has proven to get me up, three weeks and counting. But my sleepiness doesn't just end there... I even became a skilled mathematician to turn off the alarm in my sleep. The next step, or rock bottom decision, was to scan the dog food barcode, and it worked; everyday (for the last two weeks) I get up in a second, go to the bathroom and run the water, go downstairs to scan the barcode and feed the dogs, come upstairs straight to the shower (I'll have to switch the barcode once this kibble is done though, or just cut it out and leave it in the same place). Really, Alarmy has been a life saver. I can go to bed completely sure that I will wake up no matter how late or tired I sleep. PS - 'Loud Ringtone 5' is key to me. The first time I used the Alarmy was in Mexico City, I swear, I thought it was the city's Seismic Alert. This is a keeper. Issues with Essential Phone (or Android Pie): My phone is acting weird after Pie update and it will sometimes reboot during the night, causing Alarmy to not work. My soft solution was to reboot before going to sleep. HOWEVER, one day I rebooted but didn't unlock the hone after rebooting and the alarm didn't go on. Now I have to make sure to reboot and unlocking the phone before I go to sleep.

My old alarm tried to wake you up with these wambie pamby little gentle Tunes so that you would wake up in a fairytale mood. This thing won't hold your hand like a millennial parent and gently pull you into Consciousness, it full on kicks you from zero to a hundred screaming at you the whole way. text: This app doesn't fully cover my use-case, but it could by fixing one feature, which I'll explain. I like to set a series of alarms, at very specific intervals, each with a different ringtone. Because I have so many alarms I rely HEAVILY on Android's built-in "next-alarm-at" feature of the notification shade. I need this feature because if I can't easily confirm that the next alarm isn't until tomorrow, I'm likely to walk into a meeting and have one of my many backup alarms go off. Normally, once I've officially woken up, I go through the alarms and "skip-next-occurrence" on all the upcoming ones. If you do this in the default clock app, the "next-alarm-at" feature correctly shows that the next non-skipped alarm will be tomorrow. If you do this in Alarmy, it shows the time for whatever the next alarm is set to, regardless of whether it's skipped or not. Alarmy even has it's own "next-alarm-at" notification, which would be great, except it does the same thing: it shows "Next alarm is at [time] (will be skipped)". This completely defeats the purpose of the "next-alarm-at" feature. Fix this and get 5 stars.

Since getting written up countless times for being late to work, I was trying every app out there to get me out of bed. They would work for a while, then I would get used to the blaring ringtone and sleep through it. It even got to the point where I was doing math in my half-awakened state to shut off the alarm. I tried a wall-alarm across my room- woke up later in the morning with the plug in my hand, that I had apparently pulled out from the wall to shut off half-awake. It's really bad. A month ago, my boss said the next time I'm late that I'll be fired. So, I got this alarm clock app and I'm still employed. I hate it. I mean, I really hate it. I have the barcode scanner set for an item in my kitchen, so I HAVE to get out of bed. I have to. No choice. It gets my ass out of bed. So far. So yeah, five stars for that.

THE best alarm app ever. Crippling depression (boo hoo, I know) makes 
getting out of bed seem impossible some days. You're exhausted no matter 
what, you don't want to face the day, you don't care if you make it to your 
destination, much less on time, etc. This app just forces me to get up 
anyway. The alarms can be set up to be the most obnoxious thing you'll ever 
hear and you can adjust settings so that you CANNOT turn it off until you 
get up. I use the barcode feature and set it up so that if have to walk to 
my kitchen and scan a jar of nasty organic peanutbutter that I'll never 
eat. Works every time! This app has helped me in more ways than any other 
app ever has.

text:
BRILLIANT! The methods used to turn off the Alarms are genius and VERY 
effective. There's one method where you have to solve math questions and 
you can decide how many questions you want to have. You can also choose the 
difficulty of the questions. (From simple additions, to complex equations) 
There's another method where you have to shake your phone several times to 
turn off the alarm. (You also choose the amount times you need to shake. I 
recommend 80) And there's another method where you can take a picture of an 
object. (I recommended taking an picture of something in a separate room 
from your bedroom, so when your alarm goes off, you're forced to get out of 
bed to take the pictures. There'a also additional features that make the 
alarms even more effective. One feature prevents you from turning off your 
phone when while your alarm is ringing. Another feature gradually increases 
the volume of alarm every 30 seconds, so the longer you leave it ringing, 
the more louder it gets. Very effective : D

text: Best and most effective alarm app I've ever used! It's simple to use, but was well thought out. You can personalize the alarms with such detail, that no matter what your trouble is with waking up, there is a setting on here that can help you! They literally thought of everything! I have trouble hearing my alarm to wake up, and I will quickly adjust to hearing the same alarm every morning and start sleeping through it, not to mention shutting off my alarm but falling back asleep instead of getting up. Alarmy designers created extra loud tones for the heavy sleeper like me, and an option for "random play" so it will play a different tone each time it goes off so I can't adjust to it. There are also various methods to dismiss the alarm that can force you to use your thinking cap to increase awareness  and alertness, turn on the light or walk across the room or create movement to wake you all the way up. text: Helpful for forcing a better sleep schedule but needs a few tweaks.  Whatever algorithm is used for photo recognition needs some substantial improvements, it is good at recognizing patterns or simple images but suffers when trying to recognise locations or rooms. You could be taking a picture over and over again without the application recognizing it because one small object is out of place or the lighting is slightly different. This does show how accurate the software is but that kind of accuracy is not necesseraly something you need for an alarm clock.  I have many memories of spending over five minutes trying again and again to get the app to recognize an image, eventually resorting to pulling the battery out of my phone and this (though I may be remembering wrong) didn't even work sometimes as there were a few occasions when the app would start right back up into the blaring alarm after the whole system was restarted.  If I could recommend one change it would be to make the image recognition less reliant on small insignificant details so that it can be better suited for everyday use.  Overall the app has been a big help for me personally, it's a niche that's been well filled. While I can recommend it in its current form, I won't say that it's perfect as there are definitely some problems that need to be fixed.  Thanks :)
author: A Google user

text: I wanted to come back and leave a more thorough review of this app. It's literally changed my life. I've suffered from insomnia and other sleep disorders since childhood. I've always wanted to be a morning person, but I have the hardest time waking up. I always sleep through my alarms or turn them off and fall back asleep. That simply isn't an option with this app. Plus, you can customize it so that waking doesn't have to be jarring. I set 3 alarms. The first two ring with the "temple bell" ringtone on my phone. The first alarm I have to shake hard 30 times. This wakes my body up. Five minutes later the second alarm has me do a few math problems. I'm not a math person but you can set the difficulty here, so mine is set to just hard enough to get my brain working a bit. My third alarm is set to Jonathan Coulton's "Wake Up". For this one I need to scan the barcode of something I keep in my bathroom cabinet, so this one gets me out of bed. I'm never grumpy when I wake up anymore. I am really enjoying having time to wake up slowly and take my time in the morning. I'm able to get my morning coffee in well before I head into work, so I am going in much more prepared for the day. Love it!

text: Edited: I had a 1 star review because of a bug and I contacted the dev. They got back to me in a prompt manner and surprisingly rolled out an update within a week. The update somewhat fixes the issue but it definitely works for me. Previously, I was able to restart my phone while the alarm went off, even with the no power off feature turned on. Now when I restart my phone, the app does a check to see if I actually turned the alarm off. If not, it will alarm again. This means no matter how much I restart my phone, I'm still going to have to solve math problems to shut it off. Thanks for the update and GREAT app customer service!  First review: Hello.  My half asleep self figured out a way to turn off the alarm without waking up and now I have been subconsciously doing it. I have the "prevent power off" feature enabled but when the alarm is going off I am able to hold my power button and the restart button shows up for just enough time before the app overlaps it. After a couple of half asleep tries I have been successfully able to click restart and go back to sleep and the alarm Never goes off again. I'm on a pixel 2 xl. Android 8.1.0. Let me know if you need more explaining. 2 potential solutions that I thought of. 1 make the time the app overrides the power button shorter or 2 (partial fix) add a feature that asks "are you awake" in the notifications 5 minutes after the alarm was supposed to go off and if the user does not click it the alarm will sound, but then I could just click "restart phone" again. Thanks for reading and great app over all!  Sincerely, Seth Brown (PS, didn't want to post a bad review but I couldn't find an option to report bugs in app)

text: By far the best alarm clock app. I previously had an iPhone, and this was the ONLY alarm clock app I trusted. I was pleasantly surprised to find that this app was available in the Google Play store, and immediately downloaded it. I have always been terrible about turning off alarms in my sleep, so the stock alarm apps on my phone never cut it. I would find ways to cheat the alarm clocks that make you get up and walk twenty steps (I found that if I moved my arm a certain way, it would mimick steps). You would have thought with as much effort as I put in to cheating the alarms, I would just get up. But I found this app. Answering math problems has been the only true way that I can get up in the morning, because I can't cheat that with arm motions. And it is something about these math problems that make me think, thus setting this app apart from other apps. So, long story short, I will continue trusting this app to wake me up in the morning.

text: Update: DO NOT USE THIS VERSION!   It had started glitching, not responding to attempts to shut off alarm (initially via shaking). Blamed my phone and reinstalled, then noticed the same problem repeating with the math problem option, had to disassemble phone to turn it off, later noticed that the unlock screen had ad banners on it, reinstall seemed to help. Today the problem recurred with an add either utilizing or hijacking the alarm to endlessly re-inspect the same math problem with small as banners at the top and bottom of the screen. Woke up the whole household before I realized it was an ad and I could just exit it (can't do that with the app itself).  Uninstalled, huge security risk given the permissions this app needs, and a hassle to boot.  (Previous version): very well made, and the ads etc in the free version are unobtrusive and actually useful. Different "turn off alarm" styles really helpful for adjusting to how important it is to be up by a certain point, each mode is very customizable, and the temporary mute (not snooze) feature is a brilliant addition. The math problem feature doesn't seem to be effective for waking me up anymore, but I can now quickly do fairly complex arithmetic before I'm coherent enough to find my glasses, so I'll count that as a win.  Definitely recommend to anyone.

text: This is the first alarm (app and otherwise) that is certain to wake me up! I've been known to sleep through several loud alarms and turn them off in my sleep. Alarmy doesn't let me turn it off until I've taken a pre-designated picture, which I've set as something specific that requires assembly downstairs. This is life-changing!  This alarm was great for several months until this past week. Since the last update there have been issues with the camera. My phone's native camera app works just fine but Alarmy says "camera not working." The first time this happened, I had to restart my phone and thought I would have to shake it to dismiss the emergency alarm. That option never came up and it instead said I had to "tap 3000 times to dismiss." After 10 minutes and still over 2500 taps left, I had to restart my phone again and then uninstall alarmy before it went off again. It was very frustrating. I decided to give it another try and downloaded the app again last night. I double checked all the settings and saw that "shake phone" was selected for the emergency dismiss feature. There were no options mentioning "tap 3000 times to dismiss." The same thing happened this morning where the camera didn't work and I couldn't dismiss the alarm without uninstalling the app. Please fix this bug as this has previously been the only thing that can keep me out of bed long enough to wake up. I've been using my other alarms for the past week and have been almost late to work a few times. Thank you!
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Hi, Jenna Marie Beck. In latest version, Alarmy provides the 'EMERGENCY mode'. For the Emergency mode, we are setting the difficulty(amount of the tap) for the situation the users cannot dismiss the mission they set. I am really sorry for not updating FAQ tab yet. Thank you for your feedback. We will do our best to address it ASAP.

text: First of all, I'm a REALLY heavy sleeper. I stay asleep through the sounds of thunderstorms, fireworks, people being loud right next to me, and the list goes on and on. Before I downloaded this, I was sleeping through (pretty loud) alarms that I would set on my phone with the default clock app. The options it gives you to use to turn off the alarm are great for getting your mind to start working and processing things early on in the day. I use the addition option, and the cool thing about it is that it lets you choose how many problems you need to finish and how difficult you want them to be (it shows you examples of the problems you'll be getting!). I also really like the layout and design of the app, it shows you everything you need to see up front and lets you create and turn off alarms without being confusing or excessive. All in all, if you are a heavy sleeper like I am or anything seems appealing, download this app! You won't regret it! :)

text: I recommend this alarm app to anyone who has an android and tells me they struggle waking up in the mornings, and overall it is well presented and does what it intends to do.  One thing I'd say is a minor inconvenience for me personally is it still takes a few alarms to wake me up well enough to get me out of bed. Working in retail and being my store's go to guy for covering shifts, I end up having to wake up at different times, so I end up with a very confusing string of alarms that I need to turn on and off in groups. I gave five stars anyway, because that's circumstantial and not due to the app in any way. However, a feature I'd personally like to see in future is the ability to set "groups" of alarms and possibly name them. Say rather than having to modify three or four alarms for one shift, I could just set three or four different times for the same alarm to go off.  Keep up the good work!

text: On multiple occasions, the app bugged out and the alarm did not go off despite being set. There would be a symbol in my phone's notification bar indicating that an alarm is set, and it would remain there after the alarm was supposed to go off. Then when I'd open the app to see what's wrong, the notification bar symbol would suddenly disappear, and the app would pretend that no alarm had been active in the first place.  Also, ads would frequently pop into locations on the screen that contain relevant buttons that I'm about to press.  Finally, the timers do not offer seconds, and you have to add up minutes instead of just entering an exact time that you want it to count down from. You also cannot save timers, so you have to recreate them each time, which is annoying since I frequently need the same timer over and over again.  All in all, it's rather upsetting that this would be the highest alarm app in the Play Store.

text: This has been the first app to get sleepy me out of bed. Of course sleepy me still has a few tricks up his sleeve like the fact that you can turn the entire phone off if the math question is too much at 5:30 in the morning, but beyond that it's helped tremendously. I am a chronic sleep walker/talker so half the time my body reacts to an alarm clock like I'm waking up. Sleepy me can turn off alarms, delete alarms, add alarms and even problem solve his way out of getting up (such as "my phone is making noise, turn it off"). It's pretty impressive and I've been late to work and school many times in my life because of it. After practice I've figured out the best method for me: a shake alarm five minutes before I'm supposed to wake up, another basic alarm in the middle so if the shake doesn't get me up, I don't fall back into real sleep, and then a get out of bed and take a picture alarm. Two weeks has had that one going strong, even when working two jobs and going to school full-time meant that sleep was something that was written into a schedule and was where I had to pull my extra hours from. Rough times made easier by this app.

text: This is the only alarm clock that I've found that actually works for me. To say this app changed my life seems a bit dramatic. However, give credit where credit is due! This app is absolutely amazing!!   I no longer oversleep which allows me to wake up on time and take care of important matters such as handling a business. When you are in control of a business then you know oversleeping just cannot happen.   I love it so much that I switched my phone. Yes! I changed my phone for an app!!  An iphone was given to me as a gift and I ended up exchanging the iphone for Android because this app wasn't offered in the Apple app store.  My personal favorite way to wake up that I've found most effective is to take a picture. Simply you take a photo of something outside of your room (For me it was my shower). So when your alarm goes off you are forced to get up and go take the exact same photo. You can also prevent yourself from turning off your phone or uninstalling the app which is something I was bad for with other alarm apps. They also offer math problems which is also pretty effective depending on the level difficulty that you set it at. I choose this as a backup because even when I'm half asleep I manage to correctly answer all of the math questions in order to quickly turn it off and get back to snoozing. Lol.  Thankfully I've never needed the backup because the first alarm wakes me right up! Which in itself is a miracle to me. Hahaha.   Also, the way it wakes you up is very pleasant. It gently wakes you up and increases the sound little by little.   If you are bad for oversleeping or hitting snooze then this app is for you!

text: At its core Alarmy is a good mobile alarm clock. Because it's free, I don't mind it having advertisements. However, the manner used in introducing the ads is nearly unethical. If you have a list of alarms that you begin to change, an ad will be introduced amongst the alarm list and it will have a similar design to your alarms with just a different color. This ad method tricks you into clicking ads you weren't interested in. While I'm sure this works well for the developer, it comes at a cost to the advertiser who would rather pay for legitimate visitors.

text: Straightforward app.  Wakes you up in the morning.  If you properly setup this program you will never oversleep unless you have poor sleeping habits.  Everyone is different so how I use it may not work for you but here is how I use Alarmy:    Figure out when I want to wake up (usually 2 hours before work)  Subtract approximately 8 hours and make an alarm that tells me it is time to sleep (No puzzle)  Using the most annoying sounds I set three alarms within 15 minutes of when I would like to be awake with increasingly difficult puzzles.  e.g. I want to wake up at 10AM  10 - 8 = 2  Set no puzzle alarm at 1:50AM  Set low difficulty puzzle alarm at 9:45AM  Set mid difficulty puzzle alarm at 9:50AM  Set high difficulty puzzle alarm at 9:55AM  This way I am more inclined not to go back to sleep in fear of being awoken to an annoying sound that requires hard  (for a person just waking up) math to dismiss.  Also, on the plus side this app helps to keep my mental ability sharp.   Thanks for the app!  For some reason my phone did not come with an alarm clock feature.

This wouldn't be such a big deal if the app registered more than 1/10 of the shakes you actually perform.  I sat there covering the speaker, shaking my phone for about 15 minutes this morning. text: Beautiful interface, good options available and I really the fact that it has that gradually sound increasing alarm (doesn't blare out loudly in the morning) and that you can snooze the alarm for 10 seconds while you're dismissing the alarm.  If it just had 'Walk to dismiss' options then it would've been perfect.   -Multiple alarm dismiss options  -Gradually increasing sound (useful when living with roommates who want to sleep in)  -10 second snooze option while solving alarm (like you don't want the alarm to go to full volume while you're busy doing math problems)  x No 'Walk to dissmiss' options. Sometimes you just need to get out of the bed and walk around, while the phone tracks your steps.   Add the last option and I'll give this the very well deserved 5 stars.
